question: Does the bridge (z_delivered - z_ours) organise by FLIGHT LINE, or scatter within a line as much as between lines?

inputs.role: bridge per mark; supplies bridge_mm, the quantity being grouped
the DOMINANT flight line per mark, from an earlier assign_line_from_returns run; supplies the GROUPING only, never a value

params.name: population
params.value: 'marks that already carry a dominant line'
params.why: NOT a random sample and NOT chosen by value: it is whichever marks an earlier analysis assigned. The bridge records carry only the line SET in the window (most marks see two lines), which cannot group. Stated because it bounds what this can conclude, and it excludes every unassigned mark

params.name: grouping
params.why: taken as given from the assignment run; this script does no assignment

params.name: outlier_rule
params.why: no mark cut. Every group size and per-line mean is printed so a result driven by one group or one mark is visible without cutting it

masks.name: assigned_and_bridged
masks.defn: marks carrying BOTH a dominant line and a bridge. 74 bridged marks have no assignment and are NOT counted here; 0 assigned marks have no bridge

columns.line: gen1 point_source_id, the flight line, unitless
columns.mean_mm: mean bridge on that line, mm
columns.sd_mm: sd of bridge WITHIN that line, ddof=1, mm; nan for a singleton
columns.F: one-way ANOVA MS_between / MS_within of bridge_mm by line. Large F = lines differ from each other by more than marks differ within a line
columns.ICC1: (MS_b - MS_w) / (MS_b + (k-1) MS_w), k = mean group size. The fraction of bridge variance that is BETWEEN lines. Can go negative, which means no between-line structure at all; reported as computed

headline: n=14 marks on 5 lines; between-line sd 37.8 vs within-line 99.2 mm; F(4,9)=0.308 p=0.8656; ICC(1)=-0.328
